afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KSLC 210544
AFDSLC

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Salt Lake City UT
1044 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Snow showers linger across northern Utah overnight before drying
  out tomorrow.

- Freezing conditions expected tonight and tomorrow night for Zion
  and lower Washington county.

- Another weak storm is possible for Monday with snow as low as
  valley floors.
 
&&

.DISCUSSION...The axis of the trough that has been bringing 
precipitation to northern Utah is currently just to the west of 
KSLC. This is bringing the coldest 700 mb temperatures (between -9
and -10C) over northern Utah with westerly flow aloft. This has 
kept showery activity on-and-off through much of the evening. This
activity will continue, especially southeast and east of the 
Great Salt Lake which will provide some lake induced instability 
to initiate more showers overnight. These showers will be 
relatively brief, but as temperatures have cooled to near freezing
across many locations a quick dusting of snow or graupel is 
possible across area roadways. Some of the hi-res guidance does 
want to develop a more organize band around sunrise tomorrow 
morning somewhere between Salt Lake City and Davis county. If this
does develop then an inch or two of additional snow can't be 
ruled out.

High pressure redevelops over the area tomorrow which will help 
to bring drier conditions to the region, however temperatures will
remain cooler than normal by about 5 degrees. This ridge will be 
short-lived as another lower amplitude trough moves into the Great
Basin on Monday. 53% of ensemble members keep conditions 
relatively dry with this trough, while the other 47% of members 
bring light to moderate precipitation. With 700mb temperatures of
-9C with this upcoming trough there should be enough cold air to 
 support snow down to valley floors. Given that over 50% of 
 members keep conditions relatively dry there is very little QPF 
 in the 50th percentile (a few hundredths across the northern 
 terrain), however there are some wetter members. The 90th 
 percentile has 0.25-0.5" of QPF across northern Utah with a 
 favored area across Weber and Davis counties as a result of the 
 westerly flow expected with the incoming trough.

Conditions will get quiet again for Tuesday/Wednesday as a 
transient ridge develops. Guidance for the second half of next 
week is a bit more uncertain. ~50% of the members remain dry while
the other 50% bring in moisture from an atmospheric river making 
landfall in the PNW. This moisture is ushered into northern Utah 
alongside northwesterly flow. This could bring appreciable 
moisture to the mountains of northern Utah if this pans out, so it
will have to be something to watch to see which solution guidance
trends towards.



&&

.AVIATION...

KSLC...Periods of light rain/snow showers and associated lowered 
CIGS/VIS possible through 08Z or so. VFR conditions with cloud cover 
around 3-8 kft then remains, scattering out a bit through the day. A 
mid level cloud deck will then begin to shift in late Saturday 
evening into the overnight. Winds through the TAF period are favored 
to remain generally southerly with magnitudes less than 10 kts.

REST OF UTAH AND SOUTHWEST WYOMING...At northern terminals 
(especially nearer the ID border), periodic rain/snow chances remain 
into early Saturday morning. Where snow dominates, this may result 
in IFR/MVFR CIGS/VIS. Activity will then decrease into the daytime, 
with VFR cloud decks generally scattering out to an extent. Mid 
level clouds then increase later in the evening. At southern 
terminals, light winds and mostly clear to clear skies are expected 
to persist.

&&

.SLC WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
UT...Winter Weather Advisory until 5 AM MST Saturday for UTZ108.

     Winter Storm Warning until 11 AM MST Saturday for UTZ110-111.

     Winter Weather Advisory until 11 AM MST Saturday for UTZ112.

     Freeze Warning until 9 AM MST Saturday for UTZ123-124.

WY...None.
&&

$$

PUBLIC...Mahan
AVIATION...Warthen

For more information from NOAA's National Weather Service visit...
http://weather.gov/saltlakecity

alerts.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 20 at 10:48PM MST until November 21 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Periods of snow. Additional snow accumulations between 1 to
2 inches are possible.

* WHERE...The Wasatch Mountains.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Winter driving conditions are expected. Roads, and
especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and
hazardous.
